message.content:
Implement a real engine improvement in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (Nxeon migration engine): bring up Docker Compose projects whose directory is NON-STANDARD (e.g. Portainer stacks under /data/compose/<id>/), by discovering them from each running container's compose labels — not only from the wizard scan of standard app dirs. After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts` (green). Do NOT deploy/commit. Report per-change line numbers.

## Root cause (confirmed on a live source)
A source runs a compose project `webapp` via Portainer: its containers carry `com.docker.compose.project=webapp`, `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir=/data/compose/1`, `com.docker.compose.project.config_files=/data/compose/1/v11/docker-compose.yml`. The engine ALREADY captures these labels per container into `srcContainers` (`c.project`, `c.composeWd`, `c.configFiles`) and builds a `srcComposeFiles: Map<dir,string[]>` from them (search `srcComposeFiles`, `composeWd`, `configFiles`). BUT the compose bring-up loop only iterates `plan.composeDirs`, which is derived from the wizard scan's appDirs in STANDARD locations (/opt,/srv,/var/www,/home,/root). `/data/compose/1` is never scanned → not in `plan.composeDirs` → the stack is never `docker compose up`'d → its containers fall to standalone recreation and don't serve.

## The fix (three parts)
1. **Union the bring-up dir set** with the compose working-dirs discovered from container labels. Where the bring-up loop iterates `plan.composeDirs` (search `for (const dir of plan.composeDirs)` and the network/volume pre-passes that also iterate it), build `const composeDirsAll = [...new Set([...plan.composeDirs, ...srcComposeFiles.keys()])]` (dedupe, keep order: scan dirs first, then label-discovered dirs). Use `composeDirsAll` for the bring-up loop AND both pre-passes AND the `if (plan.composeDirs.length)` gate (gate on `composeDirsAll.length`). This makes a label-discovered dir like `/data/compose/1` a first-class compose project.

2. **Ensure the compose FILES exist on the target before `up`.** A label-discovered dir (e.g. /data/compose/1) is very likely OUTSIDE the customer's selected copy paths, so its compose file isn't on the target. In `composeEnvFor` (search where it resolves `srcComposeFiles.get(key)` and does `test -f` on each file, keeping only present ones), when a file from the label list is NOT present on the target, COPY IT from the source first: `mkdir -p <dirname>` on target, then pull the single file from the source (reuse the existing single-file pull mechanism — search how `preflightUnitExecs`/`copyFromSource` or `rsyncPull`/`tarPull` copy one file from source; the source connection `onSource` + the transfer helpers are in scope). Only after copying, re-test `-f`; if it still can't be obtained, fall back as today. Validate the path (must be absolute, `validPath`). This is the piece that makes a Portainer stack actually start (its compose YAML + any referenced env_file/relative files under the same working_dir may be needed — at minimum copy the config_files entries; if a whole working_dir copy is easy and safe via the existing tar/rsync helper, prefer copying the working_dir tree so relative build contexts / env files come too, but guard against copying something huge or a system path with the existing safeCopyTarget/validPath checks).

3. **Keep these containers out of standalone recreation.** The standalone filter already excludes `c.project` truthy and bind-mounts under a composeDir (search `underComposeDir`, `!c.project`). Since these containers HAVE `c.project` set, they're already excluded — VERIFY this, and also add the label-discovered dirs to whatever set `underComposeDir` checks against (so a container whose bind-mounts live under /data/compose/1 is treated as compose-owned). Ensure no container is BOTH brought up by compose AND recreated standalone.

## Guardrails
- Do NOT break the normal case: a source with only standard /opt compose dirs must behave exactly as today (srcComposeFiles for those dirs already resolves; the union just includes them once).
- Don't copy a system/unsafe path — reuse `validPath`/`safeCopyTarget`. Cap any working-dir tree copy sensibly.
- The label-discovered dir uses the same F2 projArg (`-p <sourceProject>`) resolution already in place (the source project name is `c.project`, e.g. `webapp`) — verify projArg resolves for these dirs too (it reads the same labels).
- Honest gates preserved: a stack whose services crash-loop on the SOURCE (some of this project's do) will still be reported per the N-of-M verdict — that's correct, not something to force.
- tsc clean + both tests green before you finish. Report: the composeDirsAll union point(s), the compose-file-copy logic in composeEnvFor, and how you verified standalone exclusion.

## Summary

Implemented non-standard-dir compose bring-up in `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts` by discovering compose projects from running containers' compose labels (e.g. Portainer stacks under `/data/compose/<id>`), not only the wizard scan of standard app dirs.

### Changes (final line numbers)

1. **`composeDirsAll` union** — line **6662**. Built right after `srcComposeFiles` is populated:
   `[...new Set([...plan.composeDirs, ...srcComposeFiles.keys() filtered by validPath && safeCopyTarget])]`. Scan dirs first (order preserved, deduped); label-discovered dirs validated to shell-inert absolute safe paths before any `cd`.

2. **Union wired into every bring-up site:**
   - Gate + progress count: `if (composeDirsAll.length)` and the `Bringing up N…` message — line **6814**.
   - External-network pre-pass loop — line **6825**.
   - External-volume pre-pass loop — line **6886**.
   - Main compose bring-up loop — line **6937**.

3. **Compose-file copy in `composeEnvFor`** — new helper `ensureComposeFilesFromSource` at line **6710**, invoked at line **6754** when any listed config file is missing on the target. Logic:
   - Prefers pulling the **whole working-dir tree** (so `env_file` refs and relative build contexts come too) when the dir is `validPath` + `safeCopyTarget`, not already on target, and `du -sk` on the source is within `COMPOSE_WD_MAX_KB` (512 MB, new const at line **317**). rsync first, tar-over-ssh fallback if the first config file didn't land.
   - **Backstop** copies any still-missing config file individually (parent must pass `safeCopyTarget`), rsync then tar fallback.
   - All source access is read-only (`du`, rsync/tar reads) and passes `assertSourceReadOnly`.
   - No-op for standard `/opt` dirs: their files are already present, so `anyMissing` is false and nothing is copied — normal case unchanged.

4. **Standalone-exclusion** — `composeRoots` now maps `composeDirsAll` (line **7363**), so a container whose bind-mounts live under `/data/compose/<id>` is treated as compose-owned by `underComposeDir`.

### Verification of standalone exclusion
`const standalone = srcContainers.filter((c) => !c.project && !underComposeDir(c))` (line **7369**). Label-discovered containers carry `c.project` (that's precisely how their compose labels were captured), so `!c.project` already excludes them from standalone recreation — no container is both `compose up`'d and recreated standalone. Adding the label dirs to `composeRoots` is the belt-and-suspenders cover for any container whose project label came back empty. F2 `projArg` resolves for these dirs unchanged: `projectNameFor` reads `srcProjectName` keyed by working-dir, which is built from the same containers' `c.project`.
